candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Council condemns attacks on bin crews and traffic wardens - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, A bin wagon had a brick thrown through a side window while out on its rounds in Oldham By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago Targeting bin crews and traffic wardens out doing their jobs is "unacceptable", a council has said, after a wagon had a brick thrown through its window while out on its rounds. At least one traffic warden was also said to have been targeted in the Goldwick area, Oldham Council said. Speaking after the bin wagon incident last month, a spokesperson said the wagon had its driver-side window smashed "by a resident" and a parking enforcement officer was subjected to abuse. "Our staff are working hard every day to deliver essential services for communities across the borough. These unacceptable actions not only put people at risk but also delay services for other residents," they added. The council has recently laid fresh double yellow lines and given out 273 parking fines so far this year in parts of the Waterloo Street area. "Enforcement officers are carrying out their duties to help keep our highways safe and accessible," the council continued. "Any form of verbal or physical abuse towards our staff is completely unacceptable and will not be tolerated." candidates.evidence_text: Manchester house explosion leaves man critically injured - BBC News Image source, Victor Olowoyo Image caption, A man is in a critical condition after an explosion at a house in Harpurhey By Lauren Hirst and Haider Saleem , North West Published 8 September 2026 A man is fighting for his life in hospital following a house explosion in Manchester. Fire crews and police were called to Ash Street in the Harpurhey area following the blast at about 10:20 BST. Greater Manchester Police said the man was critically injured and taken to hospital. Neighbouring properties were evacuated and a woman was also treated for what police said were thought to be minor injuries. Ash Street and Rochdale Road were closed and people have been urged to avoid the area. Image caption, Roads around the area had been cordoned off Neighbour Linda Kay, who has lived in the area for 28 years, said she thought a "bomb had gone off". "I was upstairs. I was supposed to be going on holiday this afternoon so my head was elsewhere," said the 68-year-old. "I've come down. I've just seen everything here and I thought 'my god what's happening'. "The ambulance driver came over and said there's been a really, really bad explosion. "I thought a bomb had gone off. "I did think it was bomb situation with all the response. It was quite scary." Image caption, A woman was also injured in the explosion Georgia, 16, said the explosion "shook the whole house and [there was] a massive bang". "It sounded like a car went straight through the front window," she said. "The police told me to exit my house as they didn't know whether it was safe or not." Phil Hendrick, head of North West operational delivery at gas infrastructure firm Cadent, said it was "too early to confirm a cause". "We are on site in Ash Street assisting fire and other emergency services, which is routine for an incident of this nature," he said. "Our job in an incident like this is to ensure everything associated with gas is safe. "Although it is too early to confirm a cause, there is nothing at this stage to suggest any issues with the local gas network." candidates.evidence_text: A suicide prevention charity, which received more than £1.5m of funding from the 3 Dads Walking group, has gone into administration Opus Restructuring and Insolvency said its appointment as administrators for Papyrus Prevention of Young Suicide had followed an "extended and extremely difficult period" for the charity The 3 Dads Walking, Andy Airey from Cumbria, Mike Palmer from Greater Manchester and Tim Owen from Norfolk, each lost a daughter – Sophie, Beth and Emily - to suicide. They said they found it "very difficult to accept" Papyrus was closing Chair of Papyrus trustees Harry Biggs-Davison said: "It has been almost unbearable for us trustees to have had to make the decision." Biggs-Davison, who lost his 25-year-old son Patrick to suicide, in 2015 said he took pride "in the certainty that our charity has saved and offered hope to countless young lives during the past 30 years" But he added: "After nearly two years of struggling to keep the charity alive in such a difficult financial climate, we have had to accept that we have no alternative."

candidates.lead: The actor says local people should help shape the regeneration of his hometown
candidates.evidence_text: Steve Coogan on Warwick Mill deal and Middleton regeneration - BBC News Image caption, Rose Marley and Steve Coogan are set to head up the mayoral development corporation By Kevin Fitzpatrick North West , Reporting from in Middleton Published 8 September 2026 Comedian Steve Coogan says a deal to acquire an historic cotton mill could "lead on to great things" as he helped lead regeneration plans in his hometown of Middleton, in Greater Manchester. Rochdale Borough Council said it had struck a deal to acquire Grade II-listed Warwick Mill, vacant for at least a decade, after a consultation of more than 2,000 people. The Bafta-winning actor co-chairs the shadow board setting up Middleton's proposed mayoral development corporation (MDC), which would have powers to buy land and drive development. At Middleton Arena, Coogan said residents should be involved "from the ground up", with regeneration done "with people, not to them". Coogan said Middleton wanted to build on the regeneration model used in Stockport , but "do things a bit differently here". He said consultation should involve people "from the ground up so that people feel involved". "We're doing things with people, not to them," he said. Image source, Rochdale Borough Council Image caption, The Grade II listed building stopped operating as a cotton mill in 1965 and has been vacant for at least a decade Warwick Mill was built in 1907, stopped operating as a cotton mill in 1965 and has been vacant for at least 10 years. Coogan described the building as an "eyesore", but said bringing it back into use could demonstrate that regeneration was happening. "If you can turn that around, then it's a sign and a signifier to people that things are actually moving," he said. "I think it's going to lead on to great things." Image caption, The event at Middleton Arena was to update the community on the next steps for the redevelopment plans for Middleton About a third of people who responded to the Our Town, Our Future consultation said they wanted Warwick Mill brought back into use. A study into possible future uses is continuing and residents would be consulted on final plans, the council said. It said residents would see changes within the next few months, with investment in urgent repairs, improved security and work to tidy the area around the mill. The council also hoped to acquire neighbouring London House. Co-chair Rose Marley said council leader Neil Emmott had told the event he wanted the office building demolished before Christmas. 'My reputation' Asked why he had become involved, Coogan said: "The only skin I've got in the game is my reputation." He said he would regard the project as a success if, in five or 10 years, people in Middleton felt "empowered" and believed they had participated in turning the town around. Marley, chief executive of Co-operatives UK, said shorter-term changes could include work on banking and Post Office services, safer streets and better lighting. Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig said MDCs were intended to help bring investment into towns, after investment had become easier to attract into Manchester city centre. In August, Craig announced a £20m Good Growth High Streets Fund in Middleton, aimed at supporting projects to improve high streets across Greater Manchester. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester's new council leader has said delivering more homes is an "absolute priority" as he set out his ambitions for the city Garry Bridges told BBC Radio Manchester's Joe McGrath Breakfast Show that high-rise developments had a place in Manchester's housing mix, but were not affordable to everyone The council aims to help deliver 36,000 homes by 2032, including at least 10,000 social, council or genuinely affordable homes. He did not recover and now l Oli's case is just one of a growing number of clinical negligence claims being made in England relating to A&E care. The council said almost a quarter of the affordable homes target had already been met Bridges also described rough sleeping as a "complete failure of the state and of society", with the council expecting about £2m through the government's £442m Rough Sleeping Programme Bridges, who was formally appointed council leader last week after succeeding Bev Craig, said getting the job had taken "a good few days to sink in" He described it as an "amazing honour" and said becoming leader was not something he had imagined when he first became involved in politics

candidates.evidence_text: Bury The Bury multi-storey car park that could 80 new homes built on top of it Plans have been in the offing since 2009 Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:24, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Q-Park, in Knowsley Street, Bury (Image: Google) A multi-storey car park in Bury town centre could see almost 80 new homes built on top of it The one-acre Q-Park site, in Knowsley Street, opposite the town hall, has long been earmarked for housing . Currently home to a 404-space underground car park, the structure was built to take the weight of an additional six-storey building above it However, the space above has remained vacant since the below-ground project was completed in 2009. Bury council has said the land ‘regularly attracts anti-social behaviour ’ and its current appearance is ‘detrimental to the wider street scheme’ The authority now wants to see new homes delivered on the site. Expectations are that around 77 flats could be built there Town hall bosses are proposing to dispose of the site to Watson Construction Ltd which was selected for the project through a tendering process. Watson Construction are also expected to take on the nearby project at Pyramid Park which could see around 138 homes built on it

Greater Manchester’s new mayor spoke of how Middletonians had felt forgotten for too long – and promised her backing for regeneration, with local opinions at its heart She took to the stage alongside actor and comedian Steve Coogan, CEO of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley and Rochdale council leader Neil Emmott to push forward the Middleton Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) This aims to bring Metrolink trams to Middleton; create new homes on brownfield plots; build high-quality business premises; and better public areas, roads and pathways “It’s what people actually want to see,” Ms Craig told Middleton Arena. “It’s about doing things in a collective way. A £6 oat milk latte isn’t the sign of regeneration.”

candidates.lead: She was there for the first official screening of Don’t Look Back In Anger - the Steven Knight documentary which charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s epic reunion tour .
candidates.evidence_text: She was there for the first official screening of Don’t Look Back In Anger - the Steven Knight documentary which charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s epic reunion tour . And as she explains in this review and this video synopsis , the film is an “unapologetically uplifting” film It features footage from rehearsals, backstage and onstage moments and the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in more than 20 years. And it’s these candid moments that are the most impactful and tear-jerking The film explores the profound emotional impact of the tour and what the band's music means to audiences and generations worldwide. But as Jenna explains, it was a little surreal to see two lads from Burnage walking the same red carpet as George Clooney, Orlando Bloom and Amanda Not that she got to enjoy too much glamour . After speedily writing up her review, she was forced to use a sandy beach bar toilet to put on her dress and heels for the premiere, while a colleague was forced to get changed behind an industrial sized bin. You can take the girl out The film, and its Manchester stars, received a eight-minute standing ovation. And Jenna reports that Noel even looked to be wiping tears away as Liam gleefully hyped up the crowd who were cheering them on She describes the film as “a story about friendships mended, bonds built, forgiveness over ego and the power of music”

candidates.evidence_text: Bury The Bury multi-storey car park that could 80 new homes built on top of it Plans have been in the offing since 2009 Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:24, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Q-Park, in Knowsley Street, Bury (Image: Google) A multi-storey car park in Bury town centre could see almost 80 new homes built on top of it The one-acre Q-Park site, in Knowsley Street, opposite the town hall, has long been earmarked for housing . Currently home to a 404-space underground car park, the structure was built to take the weight of an additional six-storey building above it However, the space above has remained vacant since the below-ground project was completed in 2009. Bury council has said the land ‘regularly attracts anti-social behaviour ’ and its current appearance is ‘detrimental to the wider street scheme’ The authority now wants to see new homes delivered on the site. Expectations are that around 77 flats could be built there Town hall bosses are proposing to dispose of the site to Watson Construction Ltd which was selected for the project through a tendering process. Watson Construction are also expected to take on the nearby project at Pyramid Park which could see around 138 homes built on it

He has also taken on Manchester’s housing crisis and a stark rough sleeping problem Though he steps up at a challenging time, he insists it’s also a time of tremendous opportunity View 3 Images New Manchester City Council Leader Garry Bridges (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former council estate kid who grew up in the Black Country, Coun Bridges came to Manchester for university in 2005 and never left. candidates.evidence_text: Middleton A blueprint for the future of Middleton, and not a £6 oat milk latte in sight “In places like Middleton, the next 10 years can be a good 10 years. We are not accepting decline" View 8 Images "People are proud to be from Middleton" Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 17:21, 08 Sep 2026 Updated 18:13, 08 Sep 2026 Middleton is changing, but the signs of its regeneration won’t be reduced to a ‘£6 oat milk latte’, according to Bev Craig At the Rochdale town’s arena last night (September 7), a different vision was laid out. Greater Manchester’s new mayor spoke of how Middletonians had felt forgotten for too long – and promised her backing for regeneration, with local opinions at its heart She took to the stage alongside actor and comedian Steve Coogan, CEO of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley and Rochdale council leader Neil Emmott to push forward the Middleton Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) This aims to bring Metrolink trams to Middleton; create new homes on brownfield plots; build high-quality business premises; and better public areas, roads and pathways “It’s what people actually want to see,” Ms Craig told Middleton Arena. “It’s about doing things in a collective way. A £6 oat milk latte isn’t the sign of regeneration.”

Greater Manchester Police describ A woman who was also caught up in the blast is being treated for injuries described by the force as 'minor'. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport issues new statement after 'technical issue' sparks travel chaos Hundreds of UK flights have been cancelled News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 08:00, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Manchester Airport (Image: MEN MEDIA) Manchester Airport has issued a new statement to passengers travelling a day after an air traffic control issue hit UK holidaymakers . Tens of thousands of passengers were affected by the Nats technical issue on Tuesday (September 8) According to Flightradar24, 1,300 flights to and from UK airports were cancelled on Tuesday, while more than 300 have been reported so far today (Wednesday). Manchester Airport is one of 15 which receive air traffic control services from Nats More than 100 flights were delayed and over a dozen were cancelled at the airport yesterday. Manchester Airport says operations are now running as normal following yesterday's issue However, passengers are still being urged to check the latest situation with their flights before travelling. Ten departures have been cancelled at Manchester Airport today , including three to Heathrow, where 246 flights have been cancelled today A spokesperson for Manchester Airport said: "Following yesterday's Nats air traffic control issue, the airport is operating as normal. Those travelling today should continue with their journey plans and check with their airline for the latest information on their flight, as usual

candidates.evidence_text: Bury The Bury multi-storey car park that could 80 new homes built on top of it Plans have been in the offing since 2009 Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:24, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Q-Park, in Knowsley Street, Bury (Image: Google) A multi-storey car park in Bury town centre could see almost 80 new homes built on top of it The one-acre Q-Park site, in Knowsley Street, opposite the town hall, has long been earmarked for housing . Currently home to a 404-space underground car park, the structure was built to take the weight of an additional six-storey building above it However, the space above has remained vacant since the below-ground project was completed in 2009. Bury council has said the land ‘regularly attracts anti-social behaviour ’ and its current appearance is ‘detrimental to the wider street scheme’ The authority now wants to see new homes delivered on the site. Expectations are that around 77 flats could be built there Town hall bosses are proposing to dispose of the site to Watson Construction Ltd which was selected for the project through a tendering process. Watson Construction are also expected to take on the nearby project at Pyramid Park which could see around 138 homes built on it

Bury council has said the land ‘regularly attracts anti-social behaviour ’ and its current appearance is ‘detrimental to the wider street scheme’ The authority now wants to see new homes delivered on the site. Expectations are that around 77 flats could be built there Town hall bosses are proposing to dispose of the site to Watson Construction Ltd which was selected for the project through a tendering process. Watson Construction are also expected to take on the nearby project at Pyramid Park which could see around 138 homes built on it

candidates.evidence_text: Middleton A blueprint for the future of Middleton, and not a £6 oat milk latte in sight “In places like Middleton, the next 10 years can be a good 10 years. We are not accepting decline" View 8 Images "People are proud to be from Middleton" Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 17:21, 08 Sep 2026 Updated 18:13, 08 Sep 2026 Middleton is changing, but the signs of its regeneration won’t be reduced to a ‘£6 oat milk latte’, according to Bev Craig At the Rochdale town’s arena last night (September 7), a different vision was laid out. Greater Manchester’s new mayor spoke of how Middletonians had felt forgotten for too long – and promised her backing for regeneration, with local opinions at its heart She took to the stage alongside actor and comedian Steve Coogan, CEO of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley and Rochdale council leader Neil Emmott to push forward the Middleton Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) This aims to bring Metrolink trams to Middleton; create new homes on brownfield plots; build high-quality business premises; and better public areas, roads and pathways “It’s what people actually want to see,” Ms Craig told Middleton Arena. “It’s about doing things in a collective way. A £6 oat milk latte isn’t the sign of regeneration.”

candidates.evidence_text: She was there for the first official screening of Don’t Look Back In Anger - the Steven Knight documentary which charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s epic reunion tour . And as she explains in this review and this video synopsis , the film is an “unapologetically uplifting” film It features footage from rehearsals, backstage and onstage moments and the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in more than 20 years. And it’s these candid moments that are the most impactful and tear-jerking The film explores the profound emotional impact of the tour and what the band's music means to audiences and generations worldwide. But as Jenna explains, it was a little surreal to see two lads from Burnage walking the same red carpet as George Clooney, Orlando Bloom and Amanda Not that she got to enjoy too much glamour . After speedily writing up her review, she was forced to use a sandy beach bar toilet to put on her dress and heels for the premiere, while a colleague was forced to get changed behind an industrial sized bin. You can take the girl out The film, and its Manchester stars, received a eight-minute standing ovation. And Jenna reports that Noel even looked to be wiping tears away as Liam gleefully hyped up the crowd who were cheering them on She describes the film as “a story about friendships mended, bonds built, forgiveness over ego and the power of music”

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Fears a crisis in Stockport is 'out of control' One councillor branded the situation a 'tragedy' Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:08, 08 Sep 2026 View 2 Images There were calls to build more social housing There are fears an apparent housing crisis in Stockport is 'out of control'. Between 2020 and 2025, the number of people presenting to Stockport council as homeless has increased by 1,155 - up 72 per cent Between 2019 and 2025 the number of people rough sleeping has quadrupled. Figures show Stockport is now only behind Manchester in Greater Manchester. Some £2m has been spent on temporary accommodation While the A Bed Every Night scheme does provide emergency accommodation, there is currently a waiting list The most common reasons for homelessness are either family or friends no longer willing or able to accommodate people; the end of a private rented tenancy; those leaving Home Office accommodation; and domestic abuse The local authority said that as a result of demand, it has seen a ‘sharp rise’ in hotels and bed and breakfasts being used ‘due to insufficient supply of suitable alternatives’

candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

candidates.summary: The scheme would include a mixture of one, two, three and four-bedroom homes

candidates.lead: The scheme would include a mixture of one, two, three and four-bedroom homes
candidates.evidence_text: Plans unveiled for 132-home development on land in Hale Skip to content News — Property Plans unveiled for 132-home development on land in Hale The scheme would include a mixture of one, two, three and four-bedroom homes. , and David Prior September 8, 2026 . 4:05 PM 2 min read Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Plans have been unveiled for a major new housing development on land in Hale. Prospect Homes is preparing proposals to build 132 homes on land off Dobbinetts Lane, close to the boundary with Wythenshawe. The developer has now launched a public consultation ahead of submitting a formal planning application to Trafford Council - you can access the consultation here . The scheme would include a mixture of one, two, three and four-bedroom homes, with 45% classed as affordable housing. Plans also include a new community park and children's play area, public open space and new walking and cycling routes. The site lies to the north of Dobbinetts Lane, between Brooks Drive and existing homes, and south-west of Wythenshawe Hospital. It forms part of the much larger Davenport Green area – previously known as Timperley Wedge – which has been allocated for development under the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone plan. That wider allocation envisages thousands of new homes alongside employment space, community facilities, green space and new transport infrastructure. A visual showing the proposed housing plan off Dobbinetts Lane Prospect Homes has revealed that an earlier version of its Dobbinetts Lane development contained 179 homes. That has now been reduced by 47 to 132 following what the developer describes as "extensive discussions" with Trafford Council. It says the revised scheme takes a more "landscape-led" approach, including retaining existing woodland in the north-east of the site and providing more public open space. Existing mature trees, woodland and hedgerows would be retained "wherever possible", with new trees, native hedgerows and meadow grassland also proposed. The developer says the scheme would deliver a biodiversity net gain "substantially" above the statutory minimum of 10%. The site lies to the north of Dobbinetts Lane, between Brooks Drive and existing homes, and south-west of Wythenshawe Hospital Vehicle access would be from Dobbinetts Lane through a new junction. Land alongside Dobbinetts Lane would also be safeguarded to allow for possible future improvements to the road, although details of what those improvements could involve have not yet been confirmed. New pedestrian and cycle routes would connect the development with the existing public right of way along its northern boundary and Brooks Drive to the west. Prospect Homes says a Transport Assessment and Travel Plan are being prepared and will examine the impact of the development on surrounding roads and junctions, as well as highway safety, parking and access to public transport. Drainage measures would include a 10-metre buffer from Fairywell Brook, permeable paving and rain gardens designed to manage surface water. Every home would also have access to electric vehicle charging infrastructure. Prospect Homes is part of Riverside, the not-for-profit housing and support organisation. The company says profits from its developments are reinvested in Riverside's affordable housing, homelessness prevention and community work. No planning application has yet been submitted. The developer is consulting residents on the proposals until Monday September 14, after which feedback will be reviewed and the plans finalised ahead of an application to Trafford Council. Responses to the consultation will be summarised in a Statement of Community Involvement submitted alongside the eventual planning application. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Only one local road has been confirmed so far Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford is set to receive almost £5 million towards repairing potholes and resurfacing roads – although the full list of Altrincham roads to benefit has yet to be confirmed The borough has been allocated £4.992m from a new £60m Greater Manchester Pothole Fund, announced last week by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig Trafford Council says the additional money will allow it to carry out more than 20 resurfacing schemes, alongside more than £1m of patching and surface treatments on roads requiring repair So far, Lloyd Street in Altrincham is among a small number of roads identified for resurfacing, with work planned on sub-sections of the road However, the council has not yet published the full programme of roads and locations that will benefit from the new funding, meaning further Altrincham schemes could be included when the details are finalised

Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Tatton Estate has insisted it is not promoting an 11,000-home scheme at Ashley and that all land north of the M56 has now been taken out of Cheshire East’s Call for Sites process - despite campaigners publishing a March letter in which the Estate In a 31 March 2026 letter found by Keep Ashley Green and seen by Altrincham Today , consultants acting for the Estate said land submitted in 2024 - including sites north of the M56 - was “still available”, and that work had identified longer-term potential for around 11,000 homes But Pete Crowther, chief executive of Tatton Estate, said the March letter referred back to the earlier 2024 submission “ As previously stated , the March document presented the vision for approximately 1,070 homes," he said. "Tatton Estate is not promoting an 11,000-home development and the land north of the M56 has been withdrawn from the Call for Sites process.” He said the Estate formally asked Cheshire East on 13 and 17 August to remove those historic sites. “The council has since enabled that process and all land north of the M56 has now been withdrawn.”

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

candidates.lead: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture
candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

candidates.evidence_text: A 19th century manor house in Rochdale, which has lain empty for decades, has been transformed into a café, which will formally open this weekend Nestled in the heart of Denehurst Park, the café will occupy the ground floor of Denehurst House and visitors can see it for themselves when it formally opens its doors this Saturday (5 September) More than just a café, the new venue will be managed and run by local Community Interest Company, Get Together After Serving (GTAS), and will be staffed entirely by former armed forces personnel and their families Set up by Rochdale residents, Adam Trennery, Wayne Traynor and Wayne Simms, GTAS aims to support the local veteran community in a number of ways, including through wellbeing programmes and local events and get-togethers Customers can expect café favourites like hot and cold sandwiches, cakes, breakfasts and tea and coffee, alongside generous opening hours and honest prices. The team is also hoping to team up with other local businesses to do specials on Fridays, like curry, pizza and pies. The gank was characterised by tightly packed housing, narrow passageways, high crime rates and large numbers of ‘ The site is so steep that Oldham contractors, Maysand, who delivered the work, had to devise a special pulley system with tracks and rollers to help transport the stone up the hill The team had to painstakingly remove all 122 steps, many of which had become broken and uneven, before reconstructing both the area underneath and the damaged steps using traditional sandstone, to match the existing stone. candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

candidates.evidence_text: Arcadian, the latest restaurant from award-winning chef Andrew Sheridan, has opened its doors in Didsbury Village Taking over the former Hispi site, Arcadian, which becomes the Open Restaurant Group’s eighth venue, is built around fire-led dining At the heart of Arcadian ’s kitchen is a bespoke open-fire grill, from which the restaurant takes its name, with every element of the menu shaped by cooking over wood, charcoal and open flame The 74-cover restaurant also features a private dining room for up to 12 guests, while the menu spans snacks and small plates through to larger cuts, seafood and desserts, with fire central to the way each dish is prepared The restaurant focuses on exceptional produce sourced from trusted farmers, growers and suppliers, with classical techniques employed to allow the quality of the ingredients to take centre stage. The menu will evolve regularly, keeping the offering fresh and exciting while making Each course at Arcadian will be served by the chefs themselves, including small plates such as coal-seared beef tartare, served with bone marrow toast and cured egg yolk, alongside fire-roasted prawns with grilled lemon, garlic and ‘nduja butter

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Like few before him, he’s using that hunt to think about what it means to be an artist The Yěrén – an ape-like ‘wild man’ said to roam the mountains of Hubei province – is a centuries-old fixture of Chinese folklore that resurfaced after the Cultural Revolution, when sightings multiplied into what became known as ‘Yěrén fever’ and culminated in the largest organise Emerging at a moment when Chinese society was renegotiating the place of culture and creativity, this elusive ‘wild man’ has become, for Yuan, a stand-in for the artist: “a figure both visible and othered, alternately mythologised, pursued, and misunderstood” The exhibition’s new commission, Two Improvisations: A Punk Musical , runs across two channels. He eventually rejected that move but, with Tottenham bringing in Omar Marmoush from Mancheste “At the beginning of pre-season I spoke to Richarlison and asked him if he wanted to extend his contract because I was happy to keep him with us,” said De Zerbi. “He didn’t want to. He’s a good Richarlison has spent the week training separately from the first team, but De Zerbi denied cutting the Brazilian adrift, insisting: “He decided everything. Not me, not the club.” Spurs will have deadline-day arrival Mykhailo Mudryk available for Saturday’s trip to Nottingham Forest, with De Zerbi suggesting the Ukrainian is ready to play up to 30 minutes after signing on loan from Chelsea

candidates.evidence_text: Arcadian , the latest restaurant from award-winning chef Andrew Sheridan and Open Restaurant Group will officially open its doors at 5pm today in the heart of Didsbury village Marking the fast-growing hospitality group’s eighth restaurant to date, Arcadian is its first site in Greater Manchester, bringing a new fire-led dining experience to Didsbury, with bookings open now here At the heart of Arcadian’s kitchen is a bespoke open-fire grill, from which the restaurant takes its name, with every element of the menu shaped by cooking over wood, charcoal and open flame. The 74-cover restaurant also features a private dining room for up to 12 guests, while t The restaurant focuses on exceptional produce sourced from trusted farmers, growers and suppliers, with classical techniques allowing the quality of the ingredients to take centre stage. The menu will evolve regularly, keeping the offering fresh and exciting while making the most Each course at Arcadian will be served by the chefs themselves, including small plates such as coal-seared beef tartare, served with bone marrow toast and cured egg yolk, alongside fire roasted prawns with grilled lemon, garlic and ‘nduja butter From the fire, mains to choose from include Warrendale Wagyu Ribeye, served with chilli miso butter, beef-fat chips and sesame. There’s also grilled monkfish tail with shellfish butter and charred fennel, as well as whole piri-piri chicken and a wood-fired cauliflower. For guests

Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти.
